chapter: Al Hibbler, Dakota Staton and later years
title: At the scene of the fatal wreck, and the end of the Dakota job
summary: He finds three adults dead and two girls injured, the driver barely hurt, and never goes back to Dakota Staton.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So meanwhile, while all this is happening, I'm the only one that saw it, because the guys in the car with me, all of them were asleep. And I stopped the car and jumped out, and ran over first to this car, this Mercedes-Benz. I looked in there, and I see three adults sitting in the front seat -- all three of them are dead. There are two children sitting in the back seat, two girls, and I thought they were dead, but I later learned that their backs had been broken or something. Anyway, this guy that caused all of this, he was laying over in the grass, and he kept saying, 'Somebody help me, somebody help me!' Well, to make a long story short, he wound up with a laceration on his cheek from going through the windshield; otherwise, he was completely all right.
Well, it was just a tragic day. We wound up having a trailer truck driver bring us into Philadelphia, I believe, and from there I went home, and of course, the other guys went on to New York.

But the idea of going back with Dakota after this particular incident and everything, something just fell apart, and I just never contacted her, she never contacted me. I heard that she made a trip down to I think South America somewhere, and there was mention of somebody calling me and asking me if I wanted to make it, but I was working and I refused it. But it was just one of those things in traveling that I guess most musicians at one time or another have had hazardous things happen.
